searchText: Oh yeah, we've not implemented this yet. But when we do, I imagine there will be no difference in structure to the other rpc req/resp https://github.com/ledgerwatch/erigon/issues/5884 has a bit more context. i mean it is just weird that it takes six bytes to repressent ~25000 length but maybe it has new weird prefix for lightclient stuff? So for all req-resp the encoding-header is just a protobuf varint representing the length of the payload. Its size is dynamic. https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/encoding#varints It should really only take up as many bytes as needed to represent the payload length huh that is pretty weird. the test message we are looking at has a first byte of `0x4a = 0100 1010`. dropping the MSB and interpretting it as an int just gives 74. whereas the size should be `size = 24896` Are you interpreting the varint correctly ? It seems like there might be a bug in parsing the header. This is what we use in Prysm: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/beacon-chain/p2p/encoder/varint.go#L16 since Altair (for the v2 APIs), there is an additional `ForkDigest`-context. See https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/p2p-interface.md#forkdigest-context LC uses the `ForkDigest` prefix as well (I guess it's a varint len + 4 bytes digest) it is used to determine what SSZ object is being transmitted eg if you request v2 block, the prefix tells you whether it is an altair or bellatrix block How is it different? Like, why do you need that? If the others works why not the same here? the v1 one only supports phase0 blocks light client data uses the altair format with the future-proofing (and yes, right now, there is only a single SSZ format for LC data, but it will change in the future0 if you perform a v2 block request (for post-phase0), you will also see the same prefix being added on gossip, the forkdigest is part of the individual topic so the prefix doesn't exist but lightclient topics are all v1 so they support only phase0 blocks? but still support post-altair sync committee? I see that it is what is happening, thank you! but really confusing nonetheless lol. v1 doesn't denote phase0/altair or bellatrix support. Its just the protocol version for the particular request ok nice. we are getting the correct result for the finality update topic! our first six bytes are 74, 38, 197, 139, 200, 4. the fork digest is 74, 38, 197, 139 so the varint is 200, 4. following the varint procedure, we get a binary number of `1001001000` in base 10 thats `584`, which is the SSZ size of the finality update object each topic is independently versioned yes. `ForkDigest` context, then varint size (of uncompressed data), then compressed data. Same as for altair/v2 blocks requests the varint size allows you to pre-allocate the buffer that will hold the decompressed data right. cmd/lightclient/sentinel/communication/ssz_snappy/stream.go that is what we are doing now. https://github.com/ledgerwatch/erigon/pull/5886/files. thanks <@881905303011086387>!!

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: since Altair (for the v2 APIs), there is an additional `ForkDigest`-context. See https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/p2p-interface.md#forkdigest-context

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: LC uses the `ForkDigest` prefix as well (I guess it's a varint len + 4 bytes digest)

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: it is used to determine what SSZ object is being transmitted

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: eg if you request v2 block, the prefix tells you whether it is an altair or bellatrix block
